*My Hypothesis are:
H1: Attitudes toward gender equality differ significantly across gender groups.
  Categorical IV: Sex. Continuous DV: Gender equality composite Composite items: Gender_Equality_1, Gender_Equality_2, Gender_Equality_3.

H2: Individuals reporting greater romantic intimacy with their partners report higher relationship satisfaction.
  Continuous IV: Romantic intimacy composite. Continuous DV: Relationship satisfaction. Composite IV items: Love_1 through Love_15 DV items prqc_1 through prqc_6


```{r library}
library(ggplot2)

```


```{r loadingData}

rawData <- read.csv('raw-data/data_doctored.csv')

#Making sure that data exists
dim(rawData)
str(rawData)

```


```{r checkValidity}

finishedCol <- rawData$Finished == 1#Selecting all the finished surveys (discarding non finished ones).
DATA <- data.frame(rawData[finishedCol,])#Filtering the data to have only the finished surveys.


validResponseIdIndex <- !is.na(DATA$ResponseId) # Identify valid ResponseIds
DATA <- DATA[validResponseIdIndex, ] # Filter the dataset

# Verify valid responses
if (sum(is.na(DATA$ResponseId)) == 0) {
  print("Nice, all the responses are valid!")
} else {
  print("There are some NA/NaN responses.")
}
```

```{r duration filtering}
durationRaw <- DATA$Duration..in.seconds. #Survey duration
durationFiltered <- durationRaw[!is.na(durationRaw)] #Indexes of NA survey durations

firstP <- summary(durationFiltered)[2] #this is the first quartile of the data
thirdP <- summary(durationFiltered[5]) #this is the third quartile of the data
idxForFirstQuartileDuration <- durationFiltered >= (firstP / 2) #indexes of answers with greater than or equal to first quartile / 2.
idxForThirdQuartileDuration <- durationFiltered <= (thirdP*2) #indexes of answers with smallar than or equal to third quartile * 2

DATA <- DATA[idxForFirstQuartileDuration,]#Removing responses that have less duration times than the first quartile/2.
DATA <- DATA[idxForThirdQuartileDuration,]#Removing responses that have greater duration times than the third quartile * 2.

durationDistHist <- ggplot(data=DATA,
                       aes(x=Duration..in.seconds.)) + geom_histogram(bins=100) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x="Duration in seconds (LOG Scale)", y="Counts in LOG Scale",title="Survey Response Duration Plot after filtering")

durationDistHist


```



```{r column filtering}
#The row data has 273 columns/variables. I won't be using all of them for my hypothesis.

genderEqList <- list()
for (i in 1:3){
  a <- paste0("Gender_Equality_",i)
  genderEqList[i] <- a
  
}


loveList <- list()
for (i in 1:15){
  a <- paste0("Love_",i)
  loveList[i] <- a
  
}

pqrList <- list()
for (i in 1:6){
  a <- paste0("prqc_",i)
  pqrList[i] <- a
  
}

varNames <- c("Sex", unlist(genderEqList), unlist(loveList), unlist(pqrList))

FDATA <- DATA[varNames] #Filtering data, to select the desired columns. (FDATA == Filtered data)

```



```{r filtering and recoding}
validData <- FDATA

genderListFiltering <- apply(FDATA[, unlist(genderEqList)], 1, function(x) all(!is.na(x) & (x >= 1 & x <= 7)))
loveListFiltering <- apply(FDATA[, unlist(loveList)], 1, function(x) all(!is.na(x) & (x >= 1 & x <= 5)))
prqcListFiltering <- apply(FDATA[, unlist(pqrList)], 1, function(x) all(!is.na(x) & (x >= 1 & x <= 7)))
sexFiltering <- !is.na(FDATA$Sex)

combinedIdx <- genderListFiltering & loveListFiltering & prqcListFiltering & sexFiltering
validData <- FDATA[combinedIdx, ]



# Reverse-code the gender_equality variables.
validData[unlist(genderEqList)] <- lapply(
  validData[unlist(genderEqList)],
  function(x) as.numeric(8 - as.numeric(x),
                     levels = 1:7)
)

```

```{r finding averages}

validData$avgGenderEq <- rowMeans(validData[,unlist(genderEqList)])
validData$avgLoveIntimacy <- rowMeans(validData[,unlist(loveList)])
validData$avgPrqc <- rowMeans(validData[,unlist(pqrList)])

```


#H1: Attitudes toward gender equality differ significantly across gender groups.
  Categorical IV: Sex. Continuous DV: Gender equality composite Composite items: Gender_Equality_1, Gender_Equality_2, Gender_Equality_3.

```{r plots: H1}

h1Plot <- ggplot(data = validData, aes(x = factor(Sex), y = as.numeric(avgGenderEq), fill=factor(Sex))) +

  
  labs(
    title = "Gender Equality Attitudes by Sex",
    x = "Sex",
    y = "Gender Equality Composite Score"
  ) +
  geom_violin() +
  geom_boxplot(width=0.08, box.color="white") +
labs(title="Gender Equality Attitudes by Sex", x="Sex", y="Gender Equality Composite Attitude Score (1–7)") +
  scale_x_discrete(
  labels = c(
    "0" = "Male",
    "1" = "Female",
    "2" = "Non-binary",
    "3" = "Prefer Not to Say"
  )
) + guides(fill=FALSE)+ #Closing the legend 
   scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:7, limits = c(1, 7))

pdf(file="plots/h1.pdf")
h1Plot
dev.off()

```

H2: Individuals reporting greater romantic intimacy with their partners report higher relationship satisfaction.
  Continuous IV: Romantic intimacy composite. Continuous DV: Relationship satisfaction. Composite IV items: Love_1 through Love_15 DV items prqc_1 through prqc_6
  
  
```{r plots: H2}

h2Plot <- ggplot(validData, aes(x=avgLoveIntimacy, y=avgPrqc, fill=avgPrqc)) +
  geom_point(alpha=0.1, position=position_jitter(width=0.05, height=0.05)) +
  geom_smooth(method="gam", se=T) +
labs(
    title = "Romantic Intimacy and Relationship Satisfaction",
    x = "Romantic Intimacy Composite Score (1–5)",
    y = "Relationship Composite Satisfaction Score (1–7)"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:5) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:7) +
  theme_minimal() + guides(fill=F) 

pdf(file="plots/h2.pdf")
h2Plot
dev.off()

```

#Comments:

It seems like both of my hypothesis hold. More specifically, for my first hypothesis, I was able to see different attitudes toward gender and equality.

For my second hypothesis, it was clearler to interpret, romantic intimacy directly effects relationship satisfaction.
